Scientific names have two parts, the genus and the species. The genus name begins with a capital letter, followed by the species name in small letters. The name is written in italics when printed or underlined when handwritten.

Fossils as Evidence

text:
Biodiversity Under Threat

Each species plays an important role in nature. Human activities like pollution, deforestation, and climate change are reducing biodiversity. When one species disappears, others that depend on it may also decline and eventually disappear.

Classification systems keep changing as we learn new things. For example, Aristotle's system worked for his time, but with new tools and technological advancements, scientists discovered microorganisms, which helped us understand the natural world better.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Earth's Spheres
text:
Earth's Spheres

Key terms: Geosphere, Hydrosphere, Cryosphere, Atmosphere, Biosphere

Earth is made up of interacting spheres: Geosphere (solid rocks, soil, landforms), Hydrosphere (liquid water), Cryosphere (solid water), Atmosphere (air), and Biosphere (living organisms and habitats). Changes in one sphere can affect others.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Earth's Spheres in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Solar Radiation and Earth's Heating
text:
Solar Radiation and Earth's Heating

Key terms: Solar radiation, Electromagnetic waves, Atmosphere

Solar radiation is the main source of energy on Earth. It reaches Earth as electromagnetic waves and is absorbed and scattered by gases, clouds, and dust particles in the atmosphere. The Sun's energy is concentrated mainly in the ultraviolet, visible, and infrared ranges, shaping Earth's climate and supporting life.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Solar Radiation and Earth's Heating in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Uneven Heating of Earth
text:
Uneven Heating of Earth

Key terms: Uneven heating, Latitude, Global winds, Ocean currents

The Earth's surface is not heated evenly due to its spherical shape and the tilt of its axis. This uneven heating creates temperature differences between the equator and the poles, driving global winds and ocean currents.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Uneven Heating of Earth in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Albedo and Surface Temperature
text:

Key terms: Albedo, Solar radiation, Surface temperature

Different materials absorb and reflect sunlight differently. Dark surfaces absorb more sunlight and heat up faster, while light-colored surfaces reflect more light and remain cooler. This is measured by albedo, the fraction of solar radiation reflected by a surface.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Albedo and Surface Temperature in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Urban Heat Island Effect
text:

Cities are warmer than surrounding rural areas, especially during summer and at night, due to the heat absorbed and re-radiated by buildings and roads. This is known as the urban heat island effect and can alter local climate and increase energy demand.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Urban Heat Island Effect in Grade 9 Science.

text:
Solar Radiation and Monsoon

The Earth's atmosphere has distinct layers, each with unique features. The troposphere, where most weather occurs, has decreasing temperature with height. The stratosphere, where the ozone layer is located, has increasing temperature with height due to UV absorption by ozone.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Atmospheric Layers and Role in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Atmosphere's Role in Protecting Earth
text:
Atmosphere's Role in Protecting Earth

The atmosphere protects life on Earth by absorbing incoming solar radiation, particularly harmful UV rays by the ozone layer, and trapping outgoing heat through greenhouse gases like CO2, CH4, and water vapor.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Atmosphere's Role in Protecting Earth in Grade 9 Science.

Uneven heating of the Earth's surface by the Sun drives local winds like valley and mountain breezes, as well as large-scale planetary winds and ocean currents.

metadata.topic: Uneven Heating Drives Winds and Ocean Currents

The ozone layer is crucial for life on Earth as it absorbs harmful UV radiation from the Sun. Human-made chemicals like CFCs can cause ozone loss, leading to increased UV radiation and harm to living organisms.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Biogeochemical Cycles

Biogeochemical cycles involve the continuous movement of matter and energy between the abiotic and biotic components of the Earth, ensuring essential nutrients like carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen remain available to support life.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Biogeochemical Cycles in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Water Cycle

The water cycle involves evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and groundwater movement, supporting all terrestrial and marine life.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Carbon Cycle
text:
Carbon Cycle

Key terms: carbon cycle, CO2, fossil fuels

Carbon circulates between the atmosphere (CO2 gas), biosphere (plants and animals), geosphere (carbonate rocks and fossil fuels), and hydrosphere (ocean water), forming the backbone of life.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Carbon Cycle in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Carbon Cycle
text:
Carbon Cycle

Key terms: Photosynthesis, Respiration, Fossil Fuels

Carbon moves between atmosphere (CO2), biosphere (plants, animals), geosphere (rocks, fossil fuels), and hydrosphere (dissolved CO2, marine shells). Plants convert CO2 to glucose through photosynthesis, while animals and decomposers release CO2 through respiration and decomposition. Fossil fuels release CO2 when burned.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Carbon Cycle in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Global Warming due to CO2
text:
Global Warming due to CO2

Key terms: Greenhouse Effect, Global Warming, Deforestation

Excessive CO2 intensifies the greenhouse effect, leading to global warming, melting of glaciers and Arctic sea ice, rising sea levels, and more extreme weather conditions. Human activities like burning fossil fuels and deforestation have raised atmospheric CO2 by about 35% since 1960.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Global Warming due to CO2 in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Nitrogen Cycle
text:
Nitrogen Cycle

Key terms: Nitrogen Fixation, Ammonification, Nitrification

Nitrogen gas (N2) is converted to soluble compounds that living beings can absorb through nitrogen fixation, assimilation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification. This cycle is essential for the synthesis of proteins and nucleic acids in all living organisms.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Nitrogen Cycle in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Oxygen Cycle
text:
Oxygen Cycle

Key terms: Photosynthesis, Respiration, Oxygen Production

Oxygen is produced by plants through photosynthesis and consumed by animals and decomposers through respiration. It also exists in combined forms in the Earth's crust and air as carbon dioxide. The balance between consumption and production sustains life across all spheres of the Earth.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxygen Cycle in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Human Impact on Biogeochemical Cycles
text:

Key terms: Climate Change, Ocean Acidification, Eutrophication

Human activities disrupt biogeochemical cycles, leading to climate change, ocean acidification, eutrophication, and loss of biodiversity. Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and overuse of fertilizers are major contributors to these disruptions.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Human Impact on Biogeochemical Cycles in Grade 9 Science.

Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce food and oxygen through photosynthesis. This process helps remove excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, which is important for maintaining a suitable temperature for life on Earth.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Photosynthesis and Carbon Cycle in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Excess CO2 in the Atmosphere

While plants need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, an excess of it in the atmosphere can lead to global warming and other environmental issues. This is because carbon dioxide traps heat, causing the Earth's temperature to rise.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Excess CO2 in the Atmosphere in Grade 9 Science.

Heat from the Earth's surface is lost through radiation, conduction, and convection. This process helps maintain a balance between the Earth's temperature and the energy it receives from the Sun.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Heat Loss from Earth's Surface in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Solar Radiation and Temperature Patterns

The Earth's spherical shape and rotation cause patterns of solar radiation and temperature that differ from what would be expected if the Earth were a flat disc. This includes the equator being warmer than the poles and the presence of seasons.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Solar Radiation and Temperature Patterns in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Wind Patterns on Earth

The Earth's combination of land and sea creates unique wind patterns, with winds blowing from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas. This is due to the difference in temperature between land and sea, which causes differences in air pressure.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Wind Patterns on Earth in Grade 9 Science.

title: NCERT Grade 9 Science | Carbon and Nitrogen in Food

The carbon in our food originally comes from carbon dioxide in the air through photosynthesis, while nitrogen comes from the atmosphere through processes like the Haber-Bosch method or by bacteria in the soil. Other human activities, like cooking and farming, can also add extra carbon dioxide or nitrogen to the environment.

metadata.subject: Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Carbon and Nitrogen in Food in Grade 9 Science.

Changes in monsoon rainfall patterns can be connected to changes in land use and warmer Arabian Sea temperatures. These changes can affect the number of days with heavy rain and the total amount of rainfall in a region.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Monsoon Rainfall and Climate Change in Grade 9 Science.

A rise in atmospheric temperature can affect the cryosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere. This can lead to changes in ice melt, sea levels, and the distribution and survival of different species.
